items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
Vocabulary: Places and activities in the park (e.g., park, skateboard, backpack, camera, boys, street), Clothes (e.g., hat, jacket, jeans), and familiar objects.
Grammar: Using have/has and don’t/doesn’t have to talk about possession (e.g., I have a bike. He has a skateboard.).
Grammar: Using Do you have...? and Yes, I do. / No, I don’t. to ask and answer about possession.
Numbers: Recognising and using numbers from 20 to 100.
2. Skills focus
Listening: Understanding simple questions, answers, and descriptions about people, objects, and activities.
Speaking: Asking and answering questions about possession using Do you have...?
Reading: Understanding simple sentences describing people, clothes, objects, and locations.
Writing: Writing simple sentences about possessions and using numbers in simple math activities.
items.outcomes:
1. Language use:
- Recall and identify at least 8 out of 10 target words related to people, clothes, places, and objects with 80% accuracy.
- Use at least 5 target words to describe people, objects, or activities in simple sentences with 80% accuracy.
- Use have/has and don’t/doesn’t have correctly to describe possession in 4 out of 5 sentences.
- Ask and answer “Do you have …?” using “Yes, I do.” / “No, I don’t.” in 3–4 exchanges with 80% accuracy.
2. Skills:
- Identify people, clothes, objects, and activities in short descriptions with 80% accuracy.
- Understand simple questions and answers about possession and select the correct picture or answer in 4 out of 5 items.
- Ask and answer “Do you have …?” in 3–4 short exchanges with a partner with 80% accuracy.
- Describe what people have using have/has in 2–3 simple sentences.
- Read and match at least 8 target words with the correct people, objects, or pictures with 80% accuracy.
- Understand 4–5 simple sentences about possessions and identify the correct information with 80% accuracy.
- Write 3–4 simple sentences about possessions using have/has or don’t/doesn’t have with 80% accuracy.
3. Value:
items.activities:
Support: Use picture/word cards to identify and count ocean animals/body parts; practice “Can …?” and “Let’s …” with sentence frames and guided pair work.
Extension: Ask and answer “Can …?” independently; describe abilities using full sentences; count and describe multiple objects/animals in pictures and make simple suggestions.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
Vocabulary: Rooms and places in the house (e.g., living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, yard, hall), Family Members (e.g., mother, father, brother, sister), and household objects.
Grammar: Using have/has and don’t/doesn’t have to describe what a house has or doesn’t have.
Grammar: Using There is/There are to describe rooms and objects in the house.
Grammar: Using can/can’t to talk about what people can and cannot do in different places.
2. Skills focus
Listening: Understanding simple descriptions of a house, rooms, objects, and activities.
Speaking: Describing a house using There is/There are, have/has, and can/can’t.
Reading: Understanding simple sentences about rooms, objects, preferences, and abilities.
Writing: Writing simple sentences to describe a house, family members, and activities.
items.outcomes:
1. Language use:
- Recall and identify at least 8 out of 10 target words for rooms, family members, and household objects with 80% accuracy.
- Use at least 6 target words to describe their house or family in simple sentences with 80% accuracy.
- Use have/has and don’t/doesn’t have correctly to describe what a house has or does not have in 4 out of 5 sentences.
- Use There is/There are to describe at least 3 rooms or objects in a house with 80% accuracy.
- Use can/can’t to describe at least 2 activities people can or cannot do in different places with 80% accuracy.
2. Skills:
- Identify at least 5 out of 6 rooms or household objects from a short description of a house with 80% accuracy.
- Understand simple descriptions using There is/There are, have/has, and can/can’t and choose the correct picture or answer in 4 out of 5 items.
- Describe a house using There is/There are and have/has in 3–4 simple sentences with 80% accuracy.
- Talk about what people can or cannot do in different places using can/can’t in 2–3 sentences.
- Read 4–5 simple sentences about a house and identify the correct information with 80% accuracy.
- Write 3–4 simple sentences describing a house using There is/There are or have/has with 80% accuracy.
- Write 2 simple sentences about what family members can or can’t do at home with 80% accuracy.
3. Value:
items.activities:
Support: Use picture/word cards to identify rooms, family, clothes, and food; practice There is/are and has/have with sentence frames.
Extension: Describe a family/home independently using There is/are and has/have; write 4–5 connected sentences with additional details.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
Vocabulary: School, school subjects, food, colors, places, jobs, and everyday activities
Grammar: Using What’s your name?, Where do you live?, What’s your favorite color/food?, and What do you want to be? to ask and answer personal questions
Grammar: Using What school subjects do you like? to talk about preferences
Functional Language: Using simple questions and answers to introduce oneself and share personal information
2. Skills focus:
Listening: Understanding simple questions and answers about personal information, preferences, and daily life
Speaking: Asking and answering simple questions about names, places, favorites, future jobs, and school subjects
Reading: Recognising and understanding familiar words and simple questions
items.outcomes:
1. Language use:
- Recall and identify at least 10 out of 12 familiar words related to school, subjects, food, colors, places, jobs, and daily activities with 80% accuracy.
- Use at least 6 target words to give simple information about themselves with 80% accuracy.
- Ask and answer at least 4 personal questions using the target structures with 80% accuracy.
- Give a short self-introduction including at least 4 pieces of personal information using the target language.
2. Skills:
- Identify key information such as name, place, favorite color/food, job, or school subject from short dialogues with 80% accuracy.
- Understand simple personal questions and choose the correct answer in 4 out of 5 items.
- Ask and answer at least 4 personal-information questions with a partner with 80% accuracy.
- Give a 4–5 sentence self-introduction including their name, where they live, favorite color/food, and future job.
- Read and understand 4–5 simple questions and match them with the correct answers with 80% accuracy.
- Write a 4–5 sentence self-introduction using familiar vocabulary and sentence patterns with 80% accuracy.
3. Value:
items.activities:
Support: Use picture/word cards to identify vocabulary; practice have/has, can, like with sentence frames and guided pair work.
Extension: Ask and answer questions independently using have/has, can, like; describe family, abilities, and preferences in 4–5 connected sentences.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Movement: Living things can move on their own (e.g., animals walking, plants growing toward light).
- Growth: Living things grow and change over time (e.g., a baby growing into an adult).
- Breathing: Living things take in air or other gases to survive (e.g., humans breathe oxygen, plants take in carbon dioxide).
- Eating: Living things need food or nutrients to survive (e.g., animals eat food, plants absorb water and sunlight).
- Reproduction: Living things can produce offspring or new life (e.g., animals have babies, plants produce seeds).
- Living things: are currently alive. They show characteristics such as movement, growth, breathing, eating, and reproduction. Examples include animals, plants, and humans.
- Once alive: were once alive but are no longer living. They used to have the characteristics of life, but now they do not. Examples include fossils, dead plants, and wooden furniture.
- Never been alive: They have never had the characteristics of life. Examples include rocks, plastic toys, and metals.
2. Skills Focus:
- Find differences between things that are living, that were once alive and that have never lived.
- Use seven rules to see if something is alive or not.
- Learn how to classify things.
classify objects and organisms into three categories: living, once alive, and never been alive.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Define and explain key characteristics of living things using appropriate scientific vocabulary (e.g., move, grow, breathe, eat, reproduce).
- Classify objects or organisms into three groups: living, once alive, and never been alive using complete sentences.
- Describe the differences between living, once alive, and never alive things using cause-and-effect or comparative language (e.g., “Living things breathe, but rocks do not.”).
2. Skills
- Listen and identify key characteristics of living things when presented orally.
- Read short texts or labels and determine the category of an object or organism based on the seven life characteristics.
- Write short explanations or descriptions to justify why something is living, once alive, or never alive.
- Classify various objects correctly into the three categories through hands-on or visual tasks.

items.contents:
1. Contents:
- Vocabulary: close, come in, go out, sit down, speak, stand up
- Sentence pattern:
+ ..., please!
+ May I ...? - Yes, you can. / No, you can't.
2. Skills focus: Listening & Speaking
Correctly pronounce the consonant clusters sp and st in target words such as speak and stand.
Use vocabulary related to classroom instructions, such as open, close, stand up, sit down, go out, come in and speak.
Give and follow classroom instructions using ____, please! and ask for and give permission using May I ____? – Yes, you can. / No, you can’t.
Read and write simple classroom instructions and expressions of permission.
items.outcomes:
1. Language use:
- Recall and identify at least 5 out of 6 classroom instructions from pictures, actions, or spoken prompts with 80% accuracy.
- Ask for permission using “May I …?” and respond with “Yes, you can.” / “No, you can’t.” in 3–4 exchanges with 80% accuracy.
- Use the target language to give at least 3 classroom instructions and ask for permission at least 2 times in a role-play activity.
- Recognize and pronounce the sp and st consonant clusters in speak, stand and at least 2 other target words with 80% accuracy.
2. Skills:
- Understand simple permission questions and responses and identify the correct meaning in 4 out of 5 items.
- Give and respond to 3–4 classroom instructions using “…., please!” with 80% accuracy.
- Ask and answer “May I …?” using the appropriate short response in 3–4 exchanges.
- Read 3–4 short classroom instructions or permission exchanges and identify the correct meaning with 80% accuracy.
- Write at least 5 classroom instruction words/phrases correctly with 80% spelling accuracy.
- Complete 3–4 short sentences or dialogues using “…., please!” and “May I …?” with 80% accuracy.
3. Value:
items.activities:
Support: Use picture/letter cards to identify K/k, /k/ and target words; practice “He’s/She’s …-ing” and “Is he/she …-ing?” with sentence frames and guided pair work.
Extension: Identify and pronounce target words independently; ask/answer action questions without prompts; describe pictures using complete sentences with He’s/She’s …-ing.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus
- Vocabulary about colors, shapes, activities, people, things at home, etc.
- Basic verbs (play, eat, run) in the present continuous tense (""is/are + verb-ing"").
- Preposition: on, under, in...
- Sequencing words (First, Then, Next, Finally)
- Structures:
+ Describing the differences: In this picture, S+V but in this picture. S+V.
+ There is/are ...
+ The present continuous tense of some action verbs (for example:
play, read, look at, write, laugh, go).
2. Skill Focus:
- Identify 4 differences between pictures.
- Describe individual pictures using the present continuous.
- Tell a simple story using sequencing words.
- Organize pictures in sequence and using sequencing words to narrate a simple story.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and use vocabulary about colors, shapes, activities, people, and things at home.
- Apply grammar structures (There is/are…, S + is/are + V-ing, prepositions, sequencing words) to describe actions and positions in pictures.
- Construct comparisons to explain differences between two pictures (e.g., In this picture, the boy is running, but in this picture, he is eating.).
2. Skills
- Observe and identify at least four differences between two pictures.
- Describe a single picture using the present continuous tense.
- Sequence and narrate a simple story using “First, Then, Next, Finally” and pictures in order.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus
- Vocabulary: animals, clothes, food, things in a house, action words
- Grammar structure: "A is different. Because B, C, and D are / can / can't ______ but B is / can / can't ______."
Example: "The sofa is different. Because the toothbrush, the bath, and the towel are in the bathroom but the sofa is in the living room."
2. Skills Focus
- Listening:
+ Identify familiar words and questions about people, animals, and objects.
+ Understand short questions and simple descriptions.
- Speaking:
+ Name and describe familiar objects and animals.
+ Answer yes/no and WH-questions with short, correct responses.
+ Express simple likes/dislikes and give brief personal information.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and use vocabulary related to animals, clothes, food, household items, and actions.
- Construct sentences using the structure “A is different because…” to compare and differentiate familiar objects or animals.
2. Skills
- Listen and recognize familiar words and short questions about people, animals, and objects.
- Speak to name and describe familiar items and animals using complete, simple sentences.
- Respond to yes/no and WH-questions with short, accurate answers and express basic preferences or personal information.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus: roots, stem, leaves, flowers
- Roots: The part of the plant that grows underground. Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
- Stem: The part that supports the plant and carries water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves and flowers.
- Leaves: The part where the plant makes food using sunlight (photosynthesis). Leaves also help the plant breathe.
- Flowers: The part of the plant that helps it reproduce by producing seeds. Flowers can attract insects and animals for pollination.
2. Skill Focus:
- Identify and describe the basic parts of a plant
- Understand the function of each part.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and label the four main parts of a plant: roots, stem, leaves, and flowers.
- Describe the function of each plant part using simple sentences (e.g., Roots absorb water from the soil).
- Explain how each part contributes to the plant’s survival using appropriate vocabulary and sentence structures.
2. Skills
- Listen and understand short explanations about the parts of a plant and their functions.
- Read and match vocabulary words with descriptions or pictures of plant parts.
- Write simple definitions or complete sentences to describe what each plant part does.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary
- Names of major countries: The US, Argentina, Brazil, the UK, Spain, Italy, Holland, Japan, Australia, and South Africa.
- Names of major continents: North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Australia, Africa, Oceania, Antarctica.
- Structures: What is the country? It's .........[ name of the country].
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and name major countries and continents accurately.
- Ask and answer questions using the target structure: “What is the country?” – “It’s [name of country].”
- Match country names to their corresponding continents to categorize geographical information.
2. Skills
- Listen and correctly recognize names of countries and continents when spoken aloud.
- Speak clearly and confidently when asking and answering questions about countries.
- Write simple Q&A sentences using the target language structure.
- Read country and continent names and locate them on a world map.
3. Values
- Develop curiosity and awareness about different parts of the world.
- Respect cultural diversity and understand that people live in many different countries and continents.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus
- Vocabulary related to family members: son, daughter, parents, grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins
- Adjectives: cool, soft, beautiful, tall, favorite.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and name different family members (e.g., cousin, aunt, grandparents).
- Describe people using basic adjectives (e.g., “My sister is tall and cool.”).
- Construct simple sentences to talk about family members and their qualities.
2. Skills
- Listen and recognize family-related vocabulary and descriptive words in context.
- Speak about their family members using vocabulary and adjectives accurately.
- Write short sentences or descriptions about their family (e.g., “This is my grandfather. He is tall and kind.”).
- Read short texts about families and identify family members and their traits.
3. Values
- Appreciate the importance of family and express positive feelings about family members.
- Show respect and care for their own family and others’ families by listening and sharing kindly.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus
- Capital letters rules
- Structures to introduce one's self:
+ Hi/ hello
+ I'm.......[age].
+ I'm from......[country/city]
- Structures to introduce a country:
+ What are 3 things would you tell your friends about your country?
+ It's a ..[adjective] country.
+ The capital is.....[ city].
+ It has............
+ Weather: It's hot in summer/ In winter, it's cold.
+ The traditional dish is..........[ a dish]
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Use and apply capital letter rules correctly when writing about themselves and their country.
- Construct and present simple self-introductions using sentence frames (e.g., Hi, I'm …, I'm from …, I'm … years old).
- Describe and explain basic facts about their country using targeted sentence structures (e.g., It has …, The capital is …, The traditional dish is …).
2. Skills
- Listen and understand self-introductions and country descriptions in spoken language.
- Read and recognize correct use of capital letters and key sentence patterns in simple texts.
- Write and speak short self-introductions and country presentations using appropriate vocabulary, structure, and punctuation.
3. Value
- Build confidence in expressing personal identity and cultural background.
- Foster pride and respect for their own country while learning to appreciate other cultures.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: light, grow, healthy, wilted
-  Learn that plants need light to grow and how light affects the health and growth of plants.
+ Show the plant that has been kept in the light. Point out its healthy, green leaves and strong stems.
+ Show the plant that has been kept in darkness. Point out its yellowing or wilted leaves and weak stems.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and use vocabulary (light, grow, healthy, wilted) to describe plant conditions.
- Explain in simple sentences how light affects plant growth (e.g., This plant is healthy because it had light. That plant is wilted because it had no light.).
- Compare plants grown in light vs. darkness and describe differences in appearance (e.g., The leaves are green in light, but yellow in darkness.).

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Introduce the three spelling patterns: ""a_e,"" ""ai,"" and ""ay.""
- Recognize and pronounce the /eɪ/ sound spelled with ""a_e,"" ""ai,"" and ""ay.""
- Practice listening for the /eɪ/ sound in spoken words and sentences.
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening: Ask students to listen carefully and identify which spelling pattern they hear in each word.
- Speaking: Practice saying sentences with the target words as a class, and then in pairs."
- Reading: highlightt the /eɪ/ words, focus on the correct pronunciation of the /eɪ/ sound.
- Writing: complete sentences using the appropriate spelling patterns (e.g., “The ____ (cake/ca_e) is on the table.”"
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and distinguish the /eɪ/ sound in words spelled with a_e, ai, and ay (e.g., cake, rain, play).
- Classify and apply the correct spelling pattern when completing or constructing sentences.
- Pronounce /eɪ/ words clearly and accurately in context, both in isolation and within sentences.
2. Skills
- Listen and recognize the /eɪ/ sound in spoken words and determine the correct spelling pattern.
- Read and highlight /eɪ/ words in short texts, practicing proper pronunciation.
- Write complete and accurate sentences using target /eɪ/ words with appropriate spelling.
- Speak clearly using /eɪ/ words in structured sentences during pair and group practice.
3. Value
- Develop attention to detail in both spoken and written English through focused listening and spelling.
- Gain confidence in using pronunciation and spelling strategies that help improve their overall communication skills.

items.contents:

items.section: 1.4. Plants need water & the right temperature
items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: light, grow, healthy, wilted
- Water is essential for plants to grow because it helps them take in nutrients from the soil.
- Without water, plants cannot stay healthy.
- Plants need a specific temperature range to grow well. If it’s too hot or too cold, plants can get damaged.
- Plants need water and the right temperature to grow and stay healthy.
2. Skill Focus:
- Observe the plant that has been watered regularly and compare it with the plant that has not been watered. Point out the healthy appearance of the watered plant and the dry, wilted appearance of
the plant that lacked water.
- Observe the plant exposed to extreme temperatures and compare it with the healthy, regularly watered plant. Wrong temperature can cause plants to wilt, dry out, or freeze.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and use key vocabulary (light, grow, healthy, wilted) to describe plants.
- Explain in simple sentences why plants need water and the right temperature to grow and stay healthy.
- Compare and differentiate between healthy and unhealthy plants using the target language (e.g., This plant is healthy because it has water. That plant is wilted because it has no water.).
2. Skills
- Observe and analyze the differences between watered and unwatered plants.
- Compare plants in normal vs. extreme temperatures and explain how temperature affects growth.
- Apply their understanding by classifying or describing plants as healthy or wilted based on given conditions.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: farm, field, forest, lake, mountain, path, river, town, village, waterfall
- Punctuation Marks:
+ Periods (.): Used at the end of sentences.
+ Question Marks (?): Used at the end of questions.
+ Commas (,): Used to separate items in a list or to pause within a sentence.
+ Apostrophes (’): Used to show possession or to form contractions.
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening Skills: Identifying and understanding vocabulary related to places and movement in the song and video.
- Speaking Skills: Repeating vocabulary words and prepositional phrases from the song with accurate pronunciation.
- Writing Skills:
+ Understanding the role of periods, question marks, commas, and apostrophes in sentences.
+ Adding correct punctuation to unpunctuated sentences.
+ Writing sentences with correct punctuation marks.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Recall and pronounce vocabulary related to places (farm, field, forest, lake, mountain, path, river, town, village, waterfall).
- Identify and differentiate punctuation marks (periods, question marks, commas, apostrophes) and their functions in sentences.
- Apply punctuation rules to construct clear and accurate sentences.
2. Skills
- Listen to the song/video and recognize vocabulary words related to places and movement.
- Speak by repeating and practicing vocabulary words and prepositional phrases with correct pronunciation.
- Write sentences using accurate punctuation and edit unpunctuated sentences by inserting appropriate marks.
3. Values
- Develop accuracy and responsibility in written communication by using correct punctuation.
- Appreciate the beauty of nature and the diversity of places (farms, rivers, mountains, etc.), fostering respect for the environment.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Phonemes: Long "i" sound (/i:/) represented by "ee", "ea" and "y"
- Word Families: Words that contain "ee", "ea" and "y" to form the long "e" sound.
- Vocabulary: tree, beach, country, week, please, story
- Vocabulary Examples: tree, bee, see, green, sea, eat, bead, happy, funny, sunny.
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening Skills:
+ Recognizing the long "i" sound in spoken words.
+ Differentiating between the "ee", "ea" and "y" sounds in words.
- Speaking Skills:
+ Correctly pronouncing words with "ee", "ea" and "y" sounds.
+ Repeating words and phrases that contain these sounds.
- Reading Skills:
+ Identifying the "ee", "ea" and "y" patterns in written words.
+ Reading words and simple sentences containing the long "e" sound.
- Writing Skills:
+ Spelling words with "ee", "ea" and "y"
+ Completing written exercises that reinforce the correct usage of these sounds.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Recognize and differentiate the long “e” sound (/i:/) represented by “ee”, “ea”, and “y”.
- Apply the phonics patterns to spell and construct words and simple sentences (e.g., The tree is green).
- Produce correct pronunciation of target vocabulary and use them appropriately in oral and written practice.
2. Skills
- Listen and identify words containing the long “e” sound and distinguish between “ee”, “ea”, and “y” patterns.
- Read and pronounce words and short sentences containing the target phonemes accurately.
- Write by spelling vocabulary words correctly and complete exercises reinforcing the long “e” sound patterns.
3. Values
- Build confidence in speaking and reading aloud by practicing correct pronunciation.
- Develop perseverance and attention to detail through careful listening, spelling, and recognition of sound–letter patterns.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary:
+ Ordinal numbers (1st - 30 students.)
+ Months of the year (January - December)
- Grammar Structure:
+ "When's your birthday?"
+ "My birthday is on [ordinal number] of [month]."
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening: Recognizing and understanding ordinal numbers and months of the year in spoken form.
- Reading: Identifying and reading ordinal numbers and months in written form.
- Speaking: Practicing asking and answering questions about birthdays using ordinal numbers and months.
- Writing: Completing sentences with correct dates.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Recall and pronounce ordinal numbers (1st–30th) and the months of the year (January–December).
- Construct sentences to ask and answer about birthdays using the structure When’s your birthday? / My birthday is on [ordinal number] of [month].
- Apply vocabulary and grammar structures to express personal information about dates in both spoken and written forms.
2. Skills
- Listen and identify ordinal numbers and months of the year in spoken form.
- Read and recognize ordinal numbers and months in written texts.
- Speak by practicing short dialogues to ask and answer questions about birthdays.
- Write complete sentences about birthdays using the correct ordinal numbers and months.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
⁻	Understand the elements plants need to survive and grow.
⁻	Learn and use key vocabulary: water, light, soil, air, temperature.
⁻	Learn and use key sentence structures to describe plant needs and functions.
2. Skills:
⁻	Language skills: Listening (to teacher instructions and videos), Speaking (discussions, answering questions), Reading (labels and PPT), Writing (answers).
⁻	Cognitive skills: Observation, classifying plant needs, connecting cause and effect.
⁻	Fine motor skills: Coloring, writing. Drawing.
⁻	Social skills: Teamwork, collaboration in group activities.
